units.text: 03. God, geometry and the world machine

A human law has an author. Where, then, does the law obeyed by planets come from? In a culture for which creation and divine order were central questions, the vocabulary of the cosmic legislator was not mere decoration. It offered a bridge between theology, metaphysics and the new mathematical physics.

For Descartes, matter is characterized by extension and its changes are explained mechanically. The stability of order is linked to God’s unchanging character. In Principles of Philosophy, the laws of motion do not appear merely as practical summaries of observation. They have a justification within his philosophical architecture. This confidence did not prevent some Cartesian collision rules from being wrong. A metaphysical justification strong for its author does not guarantee good physics (Descartes, 1644, partea a II-a; Slowik, „Descartes’ Physics”) .

Newton radically changes the power of mathematical unification. Principia connects celestial and terrestrial motions through a common framework of principles and demonstrations. Its importance lies not merely in writing formulas but in showing how very different phenomena can be related through explicit assumptions, approximations and comparisons with observation (Newton, 1687/1726) .

This unification contains an intellectual promise: we do not necessarily need a separate explanation for every region of the world. But the promise does not close every question. Successfully describing gravitational attraction does not, simply by writing the relationship, explain gravity’s ultimate mechanism. Newton himself distinguishes what can be deduced from phenomena from hypotheses about causes that he cannot establish in the same way.

Imagine two astronomers. The first has an intuitive story about cosmic vortices but cannot obtain sufficiently good trajectories from it. The second has a precise mathematical relationship, yet the underlying mechanism troubles him. Whom do we follow? For navigation and calculation, whoever predicts better. For the question about the nature of interaction, the dispute can continue. This is an important moment: predictive usefulness and metaphysical satisfaction can part ways.

The modern concept of law thus gains autonomy. We need not solve every question about the universe’s author to compare two models of motion. Believer and nonbeliever can share a laboratory if they accept the same procedures of measurement and correction. This is a logical possibility of the method, not a claim that the actual history of science was free of religious and political conflicts.

The machine metaphor also changes what we consider explained. If understanding means showing the parts and their interactions, purpose risks being excluded from nature and relocated to the designer. The machine has a purpose for its builder, not necessarily for its gears. Such a model clarifies many phenomena but may become too narrow when used as a premature verdict on organism, mind or society.

A historical qualification is also necessary: ‘science simply replaced religion’ is too linear a story. For these authors, mathematical, theological and philosophical questions coexist. What gradually changes also includes where evidence is demanded. A claim about trajectories can be confronted with measurements, however venerable the metaphysics from which it began.

Who benefits from this shift? In principle, anyone who can use a reproducible result without belonging to the circle that formulated it. A public relationship can weaken an authority’s monopoly over explanation. Who loses? The authority claiming that the speaker’s status suffices to decide how nature behaves. But a new risk immediately appears: mathematical expertise can be used as authority in matters calculation does not resolve.

Secularizing the method therefore does not eliminate the priestly temptation. It can change its uniform. The relevant difference is not whether the speaker wears a robe or a lab coat, but whether they show how they can be contradicted, what they assumed and how far their result extends.
